artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: Steps 1 AND 2, the secret and its grant, which this one file governs. THE SECRET: gateway/mail/commassist-bearer created out of band, ARN arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:313476888478:secret:gateway/mail/commassist-bearer-cPYbR3, VersionId 5c368b4d-d6e8-4366-8988-92f4eb4b8fcd, AWSCURRENT, rotation disabled, 64 hex characters = 32 bytes of entropy. THE VALUE NEVER LEFT ONE PROCESS: generated with secrets.token_hex(32) and handed to boto3 in memory, so it never entered argv, a file, a log, Terraform state or a commit, and only its LENGTH was printed. Deliberately not `aws secretsmanager create-secret --secret-string <value>`, which would put the value in argv where a process listing can read it. The create refused to proceed if the name already existed, so a create could not silently become a rotation; describe_secret returned ResourceNotFoundException first. Read back by DESCRIBE only -- get_secret_value was never called. gateway/mail/bearer AWSCURRENT was never written, which is why this is a SECOND secret: the mail-pull Lambda reads that one whole and a comma-joined second value inside it would break it. Step 2, under its OWN ledger. The Terraform line was already at HEAD (98501422dc, verified contained before the act). Plan graded from show -json by DECOMPOSING the policy document rather than diffing it as a string: statements 1 -> 1, Effect Allow unchanged, Action ['secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'] unchanged, Condition None unchanged, resources 4 -> 5 with ADDED exactly the commassist ARN and REMOVED []. That decomposition is the point, because the whole policy is ONE opaque attribute in the plan and '0 add, 1 change, 0 destroy' would read identically had an ARN been dropped or the action widened. Applied from the SAVED plan through safe-apply (comp-tagauthz PASSED, tombstone-gate CLEAN). Live read-back: 1 statement, 1 action, 5 resources, and ALL FOUR prior ARNs confirmed INDIVIDUALLY BY NAME rather than inferred from the count -- 5 would also hold if a prior had been swapped for the new one. Post-apply targeted re-plan: 'No changes.' The added ARN's suffix -cPYbR3 equals the ARN the create returned, so the grant names the secret that was actually made.

The release's own deploy script at the release sha -- the bytes that ran. It carries E4, the MAIL_BEARER leg hunk (a second labelled value read host-side from gateway/mail/commassist-bearer, label commassist). Host i-07dccb1615503ac99, release 91811b648ab119e73e22f8d401dd09f45b8ab19b. Step 3. safe-ec2-deploy rc=0, DEPLOYMENT COMPLETE, all three steps, from C:/tmp/og-rel29 with OPAL_AGENT_SERIAL unset, DEPLOY_BASE_REF=aa75078e1b72a28219e6148d3ec8e9bf705ea111, HALT_ACK=1, AGENT_NAME=0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z and NO HALT_OVERRIDE. PRE: live md5 read 97 identical of 97, 0 mismatch, so live WAS r28 and step 3's STOP did not apply. AFTER, via r29_verify.py --expect-changed MAIL_BEARER,MAIL_BEARER_LABELS: VERIFY PASS 5 of 5 -- /health 200 and service active with MainPID 857046 against 791928 before (the one signed restart); shipped md5 98 of 98 identical, not-ok []; tool list unchanged name for name 66 -> 66, added [] removed []; .env key names 51 -> 52 with exactly MAIL_SENDER_DOMAIN_TABLE added and none removed; and every pre-existing .env value's sha256 unchanged except the two expected, equal 49 of 51, changed exactly ['MAIL_BEARER','MAIL_BEARER_LABELS']. No .env value, bearer, token or identity was printed at any point.

The R45 fetch control, and it reads ZERO: entries_counted 6441, entries_touched_since_start 0, basis 'top level and one level down of bun's install cache; creation time OR modified time >= deploy_started_utc', with deploy_started_utc 2026-10-09T12:30:22Z. The start time was RE-RECORDED immediately before the successful attempt rather than carried from the first blocked one, so the window cannot miss a fetch by starting too late. Corroborated by an independent instrument: r29_bun_cache_size.py read bytes 1882231173 / files 115217 / dirs 13181 both before (11:36:39Z) and after (12:35:43Z) -- byte-identical and count-identical. Above 0 is a rollback trigger; it is 0, so no trigger fired.

Step 5/7, recorded BY HAND in the MAIN tree as the order requires. The wrapper's own step 3/3 did write and commit the four fields, but only inside the release worktree (ee6bafe2c6 on the detached release HEAD), and its release_note there carried OG-rl-1's older text -- so the main tree's record was the one that counted and it was stale at r28. mutant.description: Readers were shown able to go both ways. (1) The issuer recorded the pre-cut live policy at exactly FOUR resources with no commassist ARN, and the secret as not existing (describe -> ResourceNotFoundException, which my own create path re-confirmed before writing); both moved. (2) The halt gate DISCRIMINATED rather than merely passing: it refused rc=3 twice on a real premise and admitted only once that premise was true, and the admission was reached by making the premise true rather than by overriding it. (3) The bun-cache control was read by two independent instruments -- a touched-entry count and a total-bytes/file-count walk -- which agree at zero movement. (4) The .env limb is a sha256 comparison across the whole 51-key set, so it could have failed on any unexpected value and instead named exactly the two the halves signed. (5) The live md5 read distinguished before from after on its own scale: 97 of 97 against the r28 list before, 98 of 98 against the release list after.

The verify limbs read 5 of 5 and the fetch control 0 of 6441. MainPID moved 791928 -> 857046, which is the positive evidence that the service actually restarted rather than the deploy being a no-op.

surprises: NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S74: BLOCKING, ARMED, disarm_owner 2.0.0_SA_COO~O -- RESOLVED. safe-ec2-deploy's halt gate refused the r29 deploy rc=3 with 'SERIAL RESOLVES TO NO KNOWN AGENT'. Not the corrupted serial the banner guesses (od -c reads exactly '0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z\n'): the release worktree is a SPARSE checkout, so org/tier2_senior/0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z is absent from its disk while present in its HEAD commit tree, and the gate stats the disk. Nothing shipped; live md5 re-read 97 of 97 after the block. Dispositioned by A2, then by A3.

NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S75: BLOCKING, ARMED, disarm_owner 2.0.0_SA_COO~O -- RESOLVED, and it CORRECTS one half of Z-S74. Amendment A2's remedy could not work as written: safe-ec2-deploy.sh:57 overwrites HALT_GATE_REPO_ROOT unconditionally with the calling worktree, deliberately per ruling R-53, and halt_gate_validate_serial scans THAT variable alone -- the two-root loop that also reads HALT_GATE_SHARED_ROOT belongs to halt_gate_worker_issuer and runs only for 0.9.0_WK_* serials. The re-run under A2 returned the same rc=3. It also records a second finding worth carrying: step (5)'s dry-run instruction cannot catch this class, because a dry run sourced from the main checkout resolves different roots than the deploy sourced from the worktree -- mine read rc 0/0 minutes before the deploy read rc=3 on the same two limbs. A3 @3e14f27aee ruled the tested cone fix and superseded A2.
session_log: This seat is a SESSION seat, not an L7 worker subagent. Order of acts was Half 2's own: the secret, then the policy line under its own ledger, then the deploy under its own ledger, then the immediate verifies, then the manifest, then the closes, then the criteria. Every precondition was measured before the first act rather than taken from the order -- three halves and the ANNOUNCE read AT HEAD by bytes with each named commit tested for containment; both worktrees confirmed to have survived the overnight reboot at exactly their expected shas with clean trees; the live policy read at exactly four resources with no commassist ARN; the secret confirmed absent; and the live host confirmed to be r28 at 97 of 97. One ordering fact turned out to be load-bearing and was spotted in the reading rather than the hard way: gateway-read-secrets.tf resolves the new secret through a `data` source BY NAME, so a plan before the secret exists cannot resolve -- the ANNOUNCE's create-then-plan order is not stylistic. THE DEPLOY TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS AND THAT IS THE SUBSTANCE OF THIS CELL. The halt gate refused twice, fail-closed, and both refusals were correct behaviour on a wrong premise. I did not reach for HALT_OVERRIDE, which the order's BOUNDS forbid; I measured the gate down to its predicate, found that the first diagnosis (sparse checkout) was right about the mechanism while the issuer's A2 remedy could not reach it, filed that as a correcting row rather than quietly trying something else, and asked. When my own dry run had passed rc 0/0 minutes before a deploy that failed on the same two limbs, I treated the disagreement as a finding about the dry run rather than noise -- it had resolved different roots than the deploy would. The fix I proposed and the issuer ruled makes the gate's own premise TRUE rather than re-pointing or weakening it, and I verified before proposing it that it cannot reach the shipped set (the release md5 list carries no org/ path) and leaves the worktree at the release HEAD with zero porcelain. After the deploy returned I ran the three step-6 reads immediately and in order, and the manifest by hand afterwards. Nothing was closed on a prediction and no .env value, bearer, token or identity was printed anywhere in this cell.
